title: Tenali Raman and the Clues of the Lost Camel

full_text:
While traveling along the dusty highway between Hampi and Bellary, Tenali Raman and three companions were stopped by an agitated, weeping camel merchant:
'Noble travelers, have you seen my lost camel? It wandered away from my caravan last night, carrying my life’s savings!'

Tenali had never seen the camel, but having observed the trail during his walk, he asked:
'Was thy camel blind in its right eye?'
'Yes, yes!' cried the merchant.
'Was it lame in its left hind leg?'
'By heaven, exactly!'
'Was it missing one upper front tooth?'
'Yes! You have seen it!'
'Did it carry a load of sweet honey on its left flank, and a load of fine wheat on its right?'
The merchant shouted with joy: 'You know everything! Where have you hidden my camel?'

When Tenali smiled and said: 'I have never laid my eyes upon your camel, nor do I know where it is now,'
the merchant flew into a rage, seized Tenali’s robes, and dragged him before King Krishnadevaraya, accusing him of camel theft and witchcraft!

The King turned to Tenali: 'Tenali, how couldst thou describe the beast and its cargo with such absolute precision if thou hast never seen it?'

Tenali bowed with serene composure:
'Maharaj, I used no witchcraft, only the eyes heaven gave me!
First: Along the road, the thorn bushes were cropped clean on the left side of the path, while the lush branches on the right side remained untouched. A beast with two healthy eyes feeds equally on both sides; therefore, it was blind in its right eye.
Second: The footprints of three hooves were deep and firm in the dust, while the left hind hoof dragged lightly, making an uneven groove, proving lameness.
Third: Where the camel bit into the wild shrubs, a small gap of two inches was left unbroken in the center of every bite mark, indicating a missing upper front tooth!
Fourth: Along the path, swarms of black ants were busy carrying fallen grains of wheat on the right side of the trail, while swarms of buzzing flies were feasting on sweet drops of honey on the left side!
A blind man could reconstruct the camel from such plain evidence!'

Just as Tenali finished his explanation, the palace watchmen arrived leading the lost camel, which had been found grazing peacefully in a nearby ravine, with its wheat and honey intact!

The merchant blushed with profound embarrassment, fell at Tenali’s feet, and begged forgiveness.
King Krishnadevaraya marvelled at Tenali’s brilliant forensic deduction, rewarding him with a purse of gold and advising his ministers to cultivate the art of observant reasoning.
moral: Keen observation of subtle natural tracks reveals truth with forensic certainty without witchcraft.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Tenali and the Lost Camel"?
options: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?

By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
